summary: Scanned 100 TODOs. 2 critical (MCP auth missing permission/scope checks), 5 high (security gaps in guest tokens, alerts access control, missing DB validation, circular import bug), 20 medium (error handling, performance, missing features in async queries), 73 low (refactors, test migrations, cleanups). Key themes: (1) Security gaps in MCP service auth and guest token validation need immediate attention; (2) Export/import logic scattered across commands instead of centralized in models (12 instances of same pattern); (3) Frontend test migration from describe() to flat test() is widespread but trivial; (4) UUID migration creates many 'remove once rolled out' markers blocked on external timeline.

todos.text: TODO (future PR): Add permission checking
todos.reasoning: MCP auth decorator lacks permission checking, meaning any authenticated user can invoke any MCP tool regardless of RBAC roles. Direct security gap.
todos.resolution_note: Created issue for RBAC permission checking - requires architectural decisions about tool-to-permission mapping

todos.text: TODO (future PR): Add JWT scope validation
todos.reasoning: JWT tokens accepted without scope validation in MCP auth, allowing tokens intended for limited access to invoke any tool.
todos.resolution_note: Created issue for JWT scope validation - requires defining scope taxonomy and coordinating with permission checking

todos.text: TODO validate db.id is equal to self.database_id
todos.reasoning: Missing validation means SQL could execute against the wrong database silently if database_id doesn't match the resolved database object.
todos.resolution_note: Added validation that database.id matches self.database_id, raising SupersetException on mismatch
